metadata.key_test: PROSPECTIVE negotiated secession: the 2019 referendum returned 98.31% for independence (independence targeted ~2027). Safeguard I (autonomy-with-backstop heading toward dissolution) + a prospective P1 ordinal prediction - can a low-capacity micro-state (parent PNG P1=0.392, Tier 3) sustain statehood? Complexity-capacity matching for a micro-state predicts a HIGH-RISK transition. Bougainville is a SUB-STATE region -> proxied via the parent state + qualitative evidence (no standalone WGI). Outcome NOT settled -> coded prospective.
metadata.notes: Reference-based record. Papua New Guinea carries real MI v1 re-scores; Bougainville is a sub-state proxy entity with no resolved scores. 1988-1998 civil war (~15,000-20,000 dead), 2001 Bougainville Peace Agreement, 2019 non-binding referendum (98.31% pro-independence of valid ballots), independence targeted ~2027 pending PNG parliamentary ratification. Scored ~2019 vs prospective 2027+ (PNG re-scored 2019->2024). PROSPECTIVE / directional-only per the framework's MODERATE-data rule.

pre_event.event_description: The November-December 2019 Bougainville independence referendum, mandated by the 2001 Bougainville Peace Agreement, returned 98.31% for independence over greater autonomy on a ~87% turnout. The result is non-binding; under the Peace Agreement the outcome is subject to consultation between the Autonomous Bougainville Government and the national government and to ratification by the PNG National Parliament, with independence targeted for ~2027.

context.fragmentation_mechanism: negotiated prospective secession (autonomy-with-backstop heading toward dissolution)
context.backstop_details: Safeguard I configuration: the 2001 Bougainville Peace Agreement established autonomy + a referendum-backed path with the national government (Port Moresby) as the constitutional guarantor/ratifier. Here the backstop is heading toward dissolution (a negotiated exit) rather than re-absorption.

a_trajectory_ranking.prediction: [PROSPECTIVE] High-risk transition. A negotiated path to independence is plausible without renewed war, but a Bougainville micro-state built on a low parent-capacity base (PNG pre-P1 ~0.392, Tier 3) faces a fragile statehood trajectory; PNG itself absorbs governance and fiscal strain from the secession process.
a_trajectory_ranking.basis: Complexity-capacity matching for a micro-state + low parent-state P1 (Tier 3); Safeguard I (autonomy-with-backstop heading toward dissolution).
a_trajectory_ranking.falsification_condition: Bougainville achieves stable, high-capacity independence by ~2027 with no fiscal/governance crisis (falsifies the fragility call), OR the process collapses into renewed armed conflict (falsifies the 'managed/negotiated' reading).

b_violence.prediction: [PROSPECTIVE] Elevated transition RISK given low capacity and the unresolved Panguna-mine/landowner cleavages, but the negotiated framework predicts no return to the 1988-1998 scale of civil war absent a breakdown in ratification.
b_violence.agency_note: Mod8: this predicts RISK, not AGENCY
b_violence.falsification_condition: Large-scale armed conflict reignites, OR the transition completes with no instability at all.

c_convergence.prediction: N/A (parent state + sub-state proxy, not a two-sovereign comparison).

d_failure_dimension.prediction: [PROSPECTIVE] The binding constraint is institutional/fiscal capacity (P1 plus economic-structure P2): a low-capacity parent cannot easily endow a viable successor, and the prospective micro-state inherits a thin revenue base.
d_failure_dimension.note: Most exposed to post-hoc coding bias.
d_failure_dimension.falsification_condition: Any failure is driven by a non-capacity dimension, or no failure materializes.

e_fragment_count.prediction: [PROSPECTIVE] 1 prospective successor state (Bougainville). Currently 0 (referendum non-binding, ratification pending); Safeguard B (capacity gate) flags low manageability for the new micro-state.
e_fragment_count.falsification_condition: More than one successor, or a permanent return to full integration with no secession.

f_reversal_risk.prediction: N/A - not a democratic-transition reversal case.

g_suppression_mechanism.classification: N/A - negotiated/referendum-backed exit, not active suppression.

h_substate_turbulence.prediction: [PROSPECTIVE] Sub-state turbulence channelled through the negotiated process (referendum, consultation, parliamentary ratification) rather than violence; Safeguard I (autonomy-with-backstop heading toward dissolution) governs.
h_substate_turbulence.falsification_condition: Sub-state turbulence escalates into renewed armed conflict.

Papua New Guinea.outcome_summary: [PROSPECTIVE - outcome not settled] The 2019 referendum's 98.31% pro-independence result moved into a negotiated, non-violent ratification track (Era Kone Covenant 2022; consultations toward a targeted ~2027 independence) rather than renewed war - consistent with the Safeguard I 'heading-toward-dissolution' reading. PNG's own capacity slipped over the window: P1 near-flat 0.392 -> 0.393 but MI 0.499 -> 0.417 (Tier 3 throughout) as economic and governance pillars eroded, consistent with the low-capacity strain the framework flagged. Bougainville statehood is NOT yet realized; the fragility prediction is pending.
key_events: 2019 referendum: 98.31% for independence (of valid ballots), ~87% turnout
2022 Era Kone Covenant: agreed political path toward independence
PNG National Parliament ratification still pending; independence targeted ~2027
no return to large-scale armed conflict through 2024

Bougainville.outcome_summary: [PROSPECTIVE, sub-state, no WB data] Qualitative: the Autonomous Bougainville Government pursued independence through the negotiated framework; peace held; but capacity for viable statehood (revenue base, public administration, the contested Panguna mine) remains the open question the framework flags. No secession has yet occurred.

analysis.overall_assessment: PROSPECTIVE hard stress test: 4/4 applicable predictions CONSISTENT WITH EVIDENCE THROUGH 2024 (2 CONFIRMED, 2 PARTIAL/prospective), 0 falsified. The defining outcome - whether a low-capacity micro-state can sustain viable independence by ~2027 - is not yet settled and is the framework's sealed forecast for this case.
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: Safeguard I can run in the secession direction: a credible autonomy-plus-backstop architecture can channel an overwhelming pro-independence vote into a negotiated, non-violent dissolution path rather than war - but the complexity-capacity logic relocates the risk from the transition process to the viability of the resulting micro-state, built on a low parent-capacity base. A genuine out-of-sample forecast to be scored at ~2027.
